title: Source checks remove one of the two leading orbital-expansion flags in an ATNF 2.9.0 pulsar screen
abstract: We screen 93 millisecond pulsars with spin and orbital period derivatives in ATNF 2.9.0. The difference between fractional orbital and spin change cancels a shared acceleration. Under nonnegative intrinsic spin-down, a positive difference requires intrinsic orbital expansion or a measurement error. Both leading positive entries differ from their source tables. The orbital derivative for Terzan 5aw omits a factor of 10^-12. The value for J1728-4608 is 100 times its source value. Applying source values removes the first flag. This remains true with either of two inconsistent spin rows in the Terzan 5 paper. J1728 remains positive across five-error rectangles, consistent with its already known orbital variability. We find no new object or unexplained signal. The other 91 rows are not source-verified. No independent telescope data or raw arrival times are tested. The bundle includes the frozen export, source values, hashes, code, figure, and offline instructions.

display.caption: The catalog difference Q and source checks for the two largest positive entries. Source units remove the Terzan 5aw flag. Both source spin alternatives are shown. J1728 retains its known positive orbital term.
